draft.title: Hypothetical Batching: Aggregate Throughput vs. Batch Size (Illustrative)
draft.body:
This post explores a hypothetical scenario concerning batch processing for local LLMs, explicitly stating that no actual measurements were taken. The core question is how aggregate throughput might change with varying batch sizes.

In this hypothetical experiment, a batch size of 1 was associated with an aggregate throughput of 22 tokens per second. Increasing the batch size to 4 in this scenario hypothetically yielded an aggregate throughput of 55 tokens per second.

It is crucial to note that these figures are purely illustrative and do not represent real-world test results. The observed rates are aggregate values, not per-request metrics. Furthermore, per-request latency was not assessed in this hypothetical setup. These numbers are intended solely to prompt discussion on the potential tradeoffs between batch size and overall processing capacity in local LLM deployments, acknowledging the hypothetical nature of the data.
